armorer.descripcion: Buys coal and iron, and sells armor. At high levels it sells diamond armor, which comes out much cheaper than hunting for the diamonds.
armorer.notas: One of the villagers most worth levelling up: the gap between what it sells as a novice and as a master is huge.
armorer.advertencia: Ranges are the game’s own: when the villager appears, each trade rolls its price within those limits. Curing it from a zombie lowers prices further, permanently and stackably.

butcher.descripcion: Buys raw meat and sells cooked meat. Goes perfectly with any animal farm.
butcher.notas: Cooking the meat yourself and selling it cooked doesn’t pay off: pay with raw meat and keep the cooked.
butcher.advertencia: Amounts are approximate: Minecraft rolls each trade’s price within a range, and it drops permanently if you cure the villager from a zombie.

cartographer.descripcion: Buys paper and sells maps, including the explorer maps that mark mansions and ocean monuments.
cartographer.notas: Its explorer maps are the only practical way to find a woodland mansion.
cartographer.advertencia: Ranges are the game’s own: when the villager appears, each trade rolls its price within those limits. Curing it from a zombie lowers prices further, permanently and stackably.

cleric.descripcion: Buys rotten flesh and sells redstone, lapis lazuli and ender pearls. It is the safest way to get pearls without fighting endermen.
cleric.notas: Rotten flesh is good for almost nothing else, so this villager turns rubbish into useful material.
cleric.advertencia: Ranges are the game’s own: when the villager appears, each trade rolls its price within those limits. Curing it from a zombie lowers prices further, permanently and stackably.

farmer.descripcion: Buys crops and sells food. It is the easiest villager to get and the one that solves hunger in your first hours.
farmer.notas: If you plant a big field, the farmer turns your spare wheat into emeralds with no extra work.
farmer.advertencia: Ranges are the game’s own: when the villager appears, each trade rolls its price within those limits. Curing it from a zombie lowers prices further, permanently and stackably.

fisherman.descripcion: Buys string and fish, and sells cooked fish and fishing rods. Handy if you have a spider farm or fish a lot.
fisherman.notas: It also sells the compass, which you need to make maps.
fisherman.advertencia: Ranges are the game’s own: when the villager appears, each trade rolls its price within those limits. Curing it from a zombie lowers prices further, permanently and stackably.

fletcher.descripcion: Buys sticks, flint and feathers, and sells arrows and bows. Since sticks come from wood, it is the cheapest villager to trade with.
fletcher.notas: Thirty-two sticks are four logs. It is the fastest way to get your first emeralds.
fletcher.advertencia: Ranges are the game’s own: when the villager appears, each trade rolls its price within those limits. Curing it from a zombie lowers prices further, permanently and stackably.

leatherworker.descripcion: Buys leather and sells dyed leather armor and saddles. Saddles cannot be crafted, so this is one of the few ways to get one.
leatherworker.notas: If you have cows, leather is endless and this villager becomes very profitable.
leatherworker.advertencia: Ranges are the game’s own: when the villager appears, each trade rolls its price within those limits. Curing it from a zombie lowers prices further, permanently and stackably.

librarian.descripcion: The most profitable job in the game. Sells enchanted books, including treasure ones that can never come from the enchanting table.
librarian.notas: Before you trade with it for the first time you can break and replace its lectern to reroll its trades. Curing it from a zombie lowers prices permanently and stackably.
librarian.advertencia: Ranges are the game’s own: when the villager appears, each trade rolls its price within those limits. Curing it from a zombie lowers prices further, permanently and stackably.

mason.descripcion: Buys clay and stone, and sells decorative blocks: bricks, quartz and coloured terracotta. The builder’s villager.
mason.notas: Sells quartz without a trip to the Nether, which is far more comfortable for big builds.
mason.advertencia: Ranges are the game’s own: when the villager appears, each trade rolls its price within those limits. Curing it from a zombie lowers prices further, permanently and stackably.

shepherd.descripcion: Buys wool and dyes, and sells shears, beds, carpets and paintings. With a few sheep it becomes a steady source of emeralds.
shepherd.notas: Shearing a sheep doesn’t kill it and the wool grows back, so this trade is fully renewable.
shepherd.advertencia: Ranges are the game’s own: when the villager appears, each trade rolls its price within those limits. Curing it from a zombie lowers prices further, permanently and stackably.

toolsmith.descripcion: Buys coal and iron, and sells tools: pickaxes, axes, shovels and hoes, enchanted at high levels.
toolsmith.notas: Its diamond pickaxe with Efficiency saves a huge amount of digging time.
toolsmith.advertencia: Ranges are the game’s own: when the villager appears, each trade rolls its price within those limits. Curing it from a zombie lowers prices further, permanently and stackably.

weaponsmith.descripcion: Buys coal and iron, and sells swords and axes, enchanted from journeyman level up.
weaponsmith.notas: One of its enchanted diamond swords is often cheaper than making and enchanting one yourself.
weaponsmith.advertencia: Ranges are the game’s own: when the villager appears, each trade rolls its price within those limits. Curing it from a zombie lowers prices further, permanently and stackably.
